answer: No: a private name cannot be satisfied from the public mirror when the lockfile pins origin and integrity. The live resolver installed acme-internal-sdk only from https://registry.private.example/acme-internal-sdk (tree 5df1e0f8de80e04e…, payload sha256=0aeee53123952b1b…). The same name offered from https://registry.public.example/acme-internal-sdk was refused with DEPENDENCY_CONFUSION naming package, pinned origin, offered origin, and integrity; the dest tree stayed empty (44136fa355b3678a1146ad16f7e8649e94fb4fc21fe77e8310c060f61caaff8a). A lockfile without an origin pin failed closed (ORIGIN_PIN_MISSING). A known-broken highest-version mutant installed the public artifact (sha256=8908c7256237265e…, tree ae58298df780e9f8…), so the public payload is live and distinct. Production tools/marketplace lockfile schema (IMP-0084) is absent on this worktree; the measured SUT is probes/TST-0219/resolver.py. SUCCESS:TST-0219

evidence.claim: Resolver refuses to satisfy the private name from the public mirror and names package, pinned origin, offered origin, and integrity in the refusal.
Installed tree hash after the refused public offer equals the empty-tree hash; the private install census contains the private payload sha256 and not the public payload sha256.

negative_controls.description: Integrity-only lockfile is refused with ORIGIN_PIN_MISSING and writes nothing.
A resolver that ignores origin pins and picks the highest version installs the public v9.9.9 artifact, proving the public payload is live and that origin pinning is load-bearing.

question: Can a private package name be satisfied from a public mirror? PASS requires the lockfile to pin both the registry origin and an integrity hash, and resolution to FAIL when the public mirror offers a same-named package.
